root_cause.text: The use of `sprintf` without a size limit on stack-allocated buffers that were too small to hold the formatted output (e.g., a content length larger than 65535) caused a stack buffer overflow, leading to a KASAN stack-out-of-bounds write.
root_cause.evidence: The KASAN report shows a stack-out-of-bounds write in `vsnprintf` called from `sprintf` in `mangle_content_len`. The patch increases the buffer size from `char buffer[sizeof("65536")]` (6 bytes) to `char buffer[sizeof("4294967295")]` (11 bytes) to accommodate the maximum possible 32-bit unsigned integer, and replaces all `sprintf` calls with `scnprintf` (or `snprintf`) that include the buffer size to prevent overflows.

candidates.rationale: Buffer declared too small (only 6 bytes) to hold formatted content length values larger than 99999, as it only accommodates up to 5-digit numbers plus null terminator. A content length larger than 65535 (e.g., 100000) would cause overflow when later formatted via sprintf.

Direct call to unbounded sprintf writes content length into the undersized buffer from Hunk 7. Without size limit, values exceeding buffer capacity cause stack buffer overflow (KASAN stack-out-of-bounds).

vuln_statements.explanation: Unbounded sprintf writes the formatted content length into the stack buffer without a size limit. When c_len exceeds the buffer capacity (e.g., values larger than 65535), a stack buffer overflow occurs, as described in the root cause.

The buffer is declared too small (only 7 bytes) to hold the maximum possible content length value (up to 10 digits). This undersized allocation in conjunction with the unbounded sprintf causes the stack buffer overflow.

bic_trace_step.reason: The function declares `char buffer[sizeof("65536")]` (6 bytes) and then calls `sprintf(buffer, "%u", c_len)` without any size limit. The variable `c_len` is computed from `*datalen - matchoff + strlen("v=")` and can be large enough to overflow the 6-byte buffer (e.g., when c_len >= 100000). This matches the root cause: stack buffer overflow due to insufficient buffer size and missing length check. No fix (e.g., snprintf or size check) is present.
